solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suggest being like a bosom friend

definitions.meaning: to hint at something indirectly, without saying it outright
describes someone very close and familiar, as a best friend is

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to act as though they are a very close companion.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb meaning to hint and an adjective meaning very close and personal.

clue.text: Sovereign not the first character to put at risk

indicators.note: the first character of the alphabet, the letter A, is left out of the word for sovereign

parts.note: imperial means sovereign, belonging to an emperor or supreme ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch is said to be no leading figure at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like a noun, but here it is the adjective IMPERIAL; 'the first character' means A, the alphabet's first letter, rather than the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangering something is exposing it to danger, a direct synonym of the verb phrase.

clue.text: Traffic in rush heading north, then east

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word for rush is written from the bottom up

parts.note: to dart is to rush suddenly
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Directions for someone hurrying through traffic, first north and then east.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a verb means to deal or do business in goods, often illicitly.

clue.text: Dress I put on animal — careful handling results

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting clothes on a pet animal takes delicate handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' seems to be about clothing the animal, but it means arrange; 'results' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful handling of something by hand, or of a person, is this kind of deft control.

clue.text: Dog in familiar territory rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pet dog rolls over on ground it knows well.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'familiar' and the start of 'territory'; 'rolling over' turns them round, and 'in' places them inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, the same as tracking or shadowing them.

clue.text: Murders covered up by police station

indicators.note: the letters are concealed inside the words police station, spanning both

explanation.surface: Killings are hushed up by officers at the station.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, to ice someone is to kill them, so this is a gangster-speak synonym.

clue.text: Organisation not making money reluctant to embrace modern technology?

indicators.note: the word for reluctant holds the technology abbreviation in its arms

parts.note: chary means wary or reluctant
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: A non-profit body is slow to adopt new tech.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-profit body raising funds for good causes is a charitable organisation.

clue.text: Not smiling back?

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship or boat

explanation.definitionFit: One word means grim-faced and also names the rear end of a vessel.

clue.text: Getting confused, I'd see algebra as nasty

indicators.note: being muddled means these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled student thinks algebra is horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant or bad-tempered is nasty; both words describe what is not agreeable to deal with.

clue.text: Crustacean found by unimportant man crossing river

indicators.note: the river letter goes across the middle of the word for the unimportant man

parts.note: a pawn is a minor piece, used for an insignificant person
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A shellfish is discovered by a lowly man wading through a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This small edible sea creature is a decapod, one of the crustaceans.

clue.text: The thing being blocked by stone creates stir

indicators.note: the pronoun is enclosed, hemmed in, by the word for the stone

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
it is a pronoun for the thing

explanation.surface: An object stuck behind a rock causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir a liquid, or stir people up, is to shake or disturb them.

clue.text: Herb shows regret

definitions.meaning: a bitter-leaved evergreen plant once used in medicine
a feeling of sorrow or remorse, or to feel it

explanation.definitionFit: The same short word is a bitter plant and an old word for remorse.

clue.text: A plain lad going out in neoclassical style

indicators.note: the words go out of their normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A simple young man heads out dressed in old-fashioned classical taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the architect Andrea Palladio, it describes a classical, symmetrical building style revived later.

clue.text: Criticise small cathedral city in a weak manner

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or lay into someone, verbally too
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly finds fault with a little English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something feebly or unconvincingly is doing it without strength, like a limping excuse.

clue.text: Fellow having got old coped

parts.note: a fellow is a man
aged means old

explanation.surface: A man getting on in years got by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having got' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by or handle a difficulty is to cope with it.

clue.text: Berks town journalist made a beastly noise

parts.note: Bray is a village town in Berkshire (Berks), England, on the Thames
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter from a Berkshire town makes a horrible din.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey makes a harsh cry, the noise of a beast of burden.

clue.text: Fierce character protecting old soldier on horseback

indicators.note: the fierce character surrounds and shields the abbreviation for old

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce person, often a formidable woman

explanation.surface: A formidable figure guards an elderly cavalryman.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a mounted infantryman or cavalry trooper in older armies.

clue.text: Painter of hay wain against farm building

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a stable is a farm building for horses

explanation.surface: An artist's haycart leans against a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hay Wain is a famous 1821 painting of an English rural scene.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable, the English landscape artist, painted The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Church court in old city besieged by spies

indicators.note: the ancient city is surrounded by the spy agency letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: An ecclesiastical tribunal in an ancient city is surrounded by agents.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the papal court and administration of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Black boy traps one wild animal

indicators.note: the black boy, letter plus word, holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a son is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dark-haired lad catches a single wild creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The buffalo of the American plains is a large wild bovine animal.

clue.text: Tick attached to a bird now gone

parts.note: a tick and a mo are both a moment

explanation.surface: A parasite clings to an extinct bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is not the insect but a moment, MO; 'attached to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant flightless bird of New Zealand is extinct, hunted out centuries ago.

clue.text: Grumbles from head of army in place of battle

indicators.note: the leading letter is placed inside the battle site name

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a 1914 battle

indicators.note: the first letter of the word army

explanation.surface: Complaints come from the general on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints or whinges are grumbles, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Areas with military units changing sides at the front

indicators.note: the left letter at the start becomes the right letter

parts.note: legions are Roman military units

explanation.surface: Districts where army units switch allegiance on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' means swapping L (left) for R (right) at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Districts or zones of a country are areas, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Jolly good supporter opposing nothing

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
V stands for versus, meaning against
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A fan backs the side playing against a team with no score.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of applause, 'well done!', is the same cheer as 'jolly good!'.

clue.text: Opera given excellent notice when returning

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with 1 written as I

indicators.note: the word for notice comes back, written right to left

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: An opera got glowing reviews when it came back.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) becomes AI, since the digit 1 stands in for the letter I; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt is one of the best-known operas.

clue.text: Poser being stupid in pub as a bodily presence

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: being silly means the letters of the word poser are scrambled

explanation.surface: A posturing show-off acts foolishly in the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Physically present rather than by letter or phone, one's body being there.
